messages:
ben (Sales): RedwoodMed procurement returned the order form with two asks: mandatory DocuSign ID check for all signers and a 99.95% SLA with sliding credits up to 12% monthly. This is a 90-day reserved POC, est $51,200. Need quick take before I respond.

kavi (Legal): Paste the exact redline if you have it. Short answer: notarization requests or very high credit caps are tough on short POCs. We usually treat POCs differently than committed reserved capacity.

ben (Sales): They pasted: "Provider shall require DocuSign identity verification for each signer. Provider warrants 99.95% uptime; for every 0.05% below target, Customer may claim service credits up to 12% of monthly fees." No notarization mention this time, but procurement said they might escalate if credit cap not accepted.

indra (Solutions): We can enable DocuSign ID Check in the envelope. Tech note: tiny dedicated pools have more variability; committing 99.95% across a 90-day short pool is risky. Spin-up 3 business days.

marc (Engineering): Agreed. Our dedicated contract precedent is 99.5% for small reserved pools. For hosted multi-tenant we report 99.9+ historically, but we don't commit that for short isolated test pools. Also propose defining "availability" (inference API only) and measurement (rolling 30-day). Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (72h notice), customer network, force majeure.

kavi (Legal): Proposed counter language for OF/MSA: "For Proof-of-Concept engagements, Provider offers a 99.5% uptime SLA. Service credits for POCs are limited to the aggregate fees paid for the POC term. Provider accepts electronic signatures via DocuSign; DocuSign identity verification satisfies Provider's signer authentication policy. Provider is not liable for third-party identity verification failures. Any request for notarization for agreements under $250,000 will require escalation and is not a baseline POC requirement." Thoughts?

zoe (Finance): Finance ok with capping credits to POC fees. If Sales wants negotiation leverage we can offer a conditional conversion credit: if Customer signs an annual Dedicated commitment within 45 days of POC completion, Provider will issue a one-time credit equal to 7% of the POC fees (example: $3,584 on $51,200). Recommend we present dollar caps in the OF for clarity: credit cap = $51,200; conversion bonus = $3,584.

ben (Sales): Procurement will want dollar figures so this helps. I'll send the counter with those exact numbers and route DocuSign to their procurement approver + their legal, then our AE + Kavi for countersign. Kavi, can you upload the redline today?

kavi (Legal): Yes, I'll draft the redline with the 99.5% POC SLA, credit cap equal to POC fees, DocuSign clause, measurement/exclusion carveouts from Marc, and the conversion credit language. Uploading to the procurement ticket by EOD.

esign-bot: DocuSign template created: "Redwood POC OF" tpl_3307. Note: enable ID Check when requested; optional Notary addendum available for >$250k with manual approval.

marc (Engineering): I'll paste a suggested SLA carveout into the ticket: measurement = rolling 30-day window; availability = inference plane; exclusions = scheduled maintenance with 72h notice, customer network, third-party dependencies, force majeure. Also call out how credits are calculated.

ben (Sales): Plan: Kavi uploads redline, Marc adds technical carveouts, Zoe confirms final $ amounts after I lock the $51,200, and I'll prepare the DocuSign routing. If procurement reintroduces notarization or raises the cap, escalate to Legal + Sales leadership. Thanks team :thumbsup:
